races.name: goracing.co.uk Future Stars Apprentice Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Tarlac
runners_data.note: Showed a second on good ground at 6f in recent form but is a genuine hold-up horse whose natural closing style is compromised in a race already overloaded with come-from-behind types, pushing her into a midfield map position; apprentice Olivia Haines carries a 3lb claim.|
runners_data.comment: Tarlac has run over today's trip and going before, and that placed effort last time out offers mild encouragement, though he's winless in his last six starts and a mid-field ranking here suggests he faces a stiff task converting promise into something more tangible.

runners_data.name: Thank The Lord
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who has failed to place in his last four starts and whose recent form figures of 8-6-0-9-0 make him extremely hard to support; the visor is fitted but 105 days off and poor going form on standard ground are compounding negatives.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 105 days off, Thank The Lord faces a stiff task on these figures — ranked seventh of nine — though he has run over today's trip and going before, and draw two offers a handy pitch from which to find early cover.

runners_data.name: Tickets
runners_data.note: Versatile sort with a win and two places from 15 career starts on good and has placed at 6f on good going, but a true hold-up style in a field that cannot naturally accommodate closers limits the scope for a clean run; Harry Vigors takes a 3lb claim.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Tickets nonetheless showed ability with a second last time out and a second five starts back — yet fifth-place finishes in between suggest inconsistency. Fit enough at 42 days, he has distance and going experience, though the 135 lb burden is a concern.

runners_data.name: Mister Sky Blue
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a tidy record showing two places from seven good-ground starts and a second at 6f in his last five; trainer Gemma Tutty has been hitting form (2/17 in 14 days) and Conor Whiteley has course knowledge to deploy his tracking style effectively.|
runners_data.comment: Mister Sky Blue shaped with promise when second four starts back and arrives here fit off a 16-day break, with experience over today's trip and going and our rating of 58 pointing to unexploited potential; the risk is he remains winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Mrs Trump
runners_data.note: Consistent class-level performer with two wins and three places from 12 runs on good going, but has not finished better than fifth in her last five starts; nine days since last run is fine, though Paul Midgley's 0/23 in 14 days is a stark trainer stat to note.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Mrs Trump faces a stiff task here — a sequence of mid-division finishes and a trainer yet to strike in 23 recent attempts make her hard to fancy, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a quick turnaround.

runners_data.name: Newyorkstateofmind
runners_data.note: Experienced nine-year-old and a natural hold-up horse whose late-running game is curtailed here because there are too many closers for all to get their natural rear draw; Ruth Carr has been active (5/27 in 14 days) and the blinkers sharpen his focus.|
runners_data.comment: Newyorkstateofmind heads into this off a 32-day break with distance and going experience to call on, and our rating of 58 marks him out as the one to beat in this field. Winless in his last six starts, but that fourth two runs back hints at residual ability worth respecting.

runners_data.name: Drish Samphire
runners_data.note: Has a noted tendency to fade in the finish and his last five runs show no win or place, predominantly on standard going where his form is poor; only seven days since last run suggests connections are trying to find an opening, but this profile is among the weakest in the field.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Drish Samphire has shown little encouragement with finishes of sixth, sixth, seventh and eighth in recent outings, and ranked last on our figures here, she's hard to fancy despite experience over today's trip and going, and a quick turnaround keeping her fresh.

runners_data.name: Golden Prosperity
runners_data.note: The one confirmed front-runner and the race's key pace-setter; 12/15 good-going starts with two wins and five places underlines his suitability and he commands the race from the front at Thirsk over 6f — Jake Dickson's 3lb claim keeps the weight manageable.|
runners_data.comment: Twice placed in his last four starts, Golden Prosperity arrives here in sharp order just nine days after his latest run, has experience over today's trip and conditions, and our rating of 55 puts him 6lb above his official rating of 49; the concern is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Hurstwood
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old prominent racer who has been placed four times from 11 runs on good going and consistently performs at this track over 6f; Peter Niven's 0/5 in 14 days is modest but the horse's course profile and tracking style are naturally suited to following Golden Prosperity.|
runners_data.comment: Hurstwood has run over today's trip and going before and ran a solid fourth last time out, just 20 days ago, so fitness isn't a concern — yet he remains winless in recent starts, and that lack of a breakthrough is the obvious question mark against him here.

races.paceDynamic: Golden Prosperity is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no serious challenger likely to dispute the lead aggressively, she should be able to dictate a comfortable, measured gallop from the front on good ground at Thirsk over 6f. Mister Sky Blue and Hurstwood are the prominent types who will look to track her, creating a small lead group but not a frantic early pace — this is a race where the tempo is controlled rather than contested. The field carries considerably more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate naturally; Tarlac, Drish Samphire, and Newyorkstateofmind are true come-from-behind types but, with so many others forced to race further forward than ideal, they are mapped to midfield positions they would not ordinarily occupy. A sustainable, front-runner-friendly gallop with a small prominent group dictating terms strongly favours horses racing on or near the pace — Golden Prosperity and those tracking her in the Mister Sky Blue/Hurstwood mould are best placed, while genuine hold-up horses are structurally compromised by the race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Golden Prosperity gets a soft lead and converts a steady gallop into a sustained run to the line.
scenarios.body: Golden Prosperity dictates every fraction unchallenged, setting a manageable pace that plays directly to her stamina and course form at Thirsk over 6f; her 12/15 good-going record and five places from recent similar assignments underline her suitability. The prominent trackers Mister Sky Blue and Hurstwood are best placed to chase her home, as they sit closest to the pace without burning energy fighting for position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Golden Prosperity's early pace is marginally faster than comfortable and one of the prominent trackers swoops past her inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Mister Sky Blue, with course form and a live trainer (2/17 in 14 days) has the profile to sit a length or two off the pace and time a run perfectly; Hurstwood has made the frame four times at Thirsk's 6f trip showing he handles the track well. Both benefit from the honest, non-frantic gallop and can produce a clean finishing effort without needing to come from off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to string the field out and open a gap for a closer weaving through.
scenarios.body: Tarlac has the most compelling recent form in this field with a second on good ground and represents the best hold-up profile despite being mapped to midfield; the key is whether the gallop is brisk enough to find a gap late. Tickets also has placed form at 6f on good and represents the trainer Patrick Neville's best chance of a late swoop if the setup allows.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Collapses Into Moderate Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Golden Prosperity underperforms early and the race loses its shape entirely, becoming a messy affair with no true pace.
scenarios.body: Without a genuine pace-setter to organise the race, bunching and traffic trouble become the defining factor and any horse with a clean passage could prevail; this scenario is the least likely given Golden Prosperity's consistent front-running profile. Mrs Trump's in-form handler Paul Midgley and Newyorkstateofmind's experience of getting competitive positions late give them residual claims in chaos.

watchPoints.text: Golden Prosperity is the pace axis — if she breaks cleanly and settles immediately, she controls the tempo and the race shape is set; watch her out of the stalls as any hesitation invites Mister Sky Blue to press.

Tarlac and Newyorkstateofmind are natural closers forced into midfield mapping by field composition — if both drift wide seeking room in the final 2f, they risk interfering with each other and blocking Tickets' run.

Drish Samphire's flagged tendency to fade in the finish combined with a run just seven days ago means she could be a significant traffic obstacle in the final furlong if she weakens sharply across the track.

Mister Sky Blue's trainer Gemma Tutty is in form (2/17 in 14 days) — any drifting in the market from this horse should be noted as the prominent-tracking profile is perfectly shaped for this race setup.

Thank The Lord runs in a visor and is returning after 105 days off for a trainer showing 0/5 in 14 days — at OR 48 in a classified stakes, his chance appears remote but monitor for any market move that would suggest connections have found a confidence-boosting target.

races.name: Bob Vickery Memorial Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)
Peter Bell Memorial Fillies' Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Bymiddaytomorrow
runners_data.note: Won over this exact 7f Good-ground combination last time out giving her strong course-and-distance form, but the STYLE_FIT flag tempers enthusiasm — she is tagged as racing somewhat out of role at prominent, and Ashley Lewis (3lb claimer) will need to be positive from the off to secure the position her race plan demands.
runners_data.comment: Bymiddaytomorrow comes here on the back of a win last time out and a trainer firing at 26% in the last fortnight — a potent combination. She has run over today's trip before, carries 141 lb from stall one, and our rating puts her clear at the head of this six-runner field.

runners_data.name: Gerry's Darling
runners_data.note: Kevin Stott rides a filly who has run four times over 7f on Good ground and placed twice, showing consistent improvement; her back-to-back 2nd and 1st over this trip mark her as the most course-and-distance proven runner in the field and she is ideally drawn to sit just behind the leader.
runners_data.comment: Gerry's Darling arrives in cracking nick — a winner last time out and second two starts back, and she has experience over today's trip and conditions. Carrying 134 lb from stall 5 is the concern, but her recent form makes her a serious threat.

runners_data.name: Love Tanya
runners_data.note: Oisin Orr partners a filly with only two runs, both placing on Good ground, suggesting she is still on a learning curve; her hold-up style is authentic and she is likely to finish well from off the pace, but she needs either stronger pace or a slightly longer trip to fully unlock her late run.
runners_data.comment: Twice placed in her last two starts, Love Tanya arrives here on a sharp 14-day turnaround with distance experience in her favour — a consistent threat despite being yet to win. The main risk is that our rating of 64 leaves her with something to find against the top-rated runners.

runners_data.name: Consultation
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe sends a filly stepping up from 6f after three runs, all on Good ground, with consistent placed form; the 42-day layoff is worth monitoring, but prominent-style horses who track well tend to handle this Thirsk layout and she gets in on a competitive mark if fit.

runners_data.name: Bonjour Belle
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's filly is, by nature, a genuine hold-up type whose last three runs all came over 7f with modest figures — she has been shifted toward midfield on the map because the rear is already congested with closers, and that compromised position makes it hard to see how she builds on an OR of 55.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, Bonjour Belle heads here having finished no better than fifth in recent outings, and while she has run over today's trip before, it's hard to make a case at these weights against stronger-rated rivals.

runners_data.name: Priscilla's Hope
runners_data.note: Five runs across 5f and 6f make this her first attempt at 7f, which could suit given she already showed a place at 6f on Good; Andrew Mullen rides and the Philip McBride yard is quiet at present (0/2 in 14 days), so she is interesting on the step up but needs things to fall right from the back.
runners_data.comment: Priscilla's Hope has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating of 64 puts her clear of her official mark — a solid case for improvement, though she remains winless in her last five starts and that consistency concern is the main risk.

runners_data.name: Spirit of Mary
runners_data.note: Ben Haslam's filly has placed twice on Good ground over 6f and brings solid exposed form, but her OR of 45 is the lowest in the field and, as a hold-up type pushed into midfield on the map by the crowded rear, she is racing in a less-than-ideal configuration for her true closing style.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Spirit of Mary nevertheless shows some consistency with thirds in her two most recent outings, and she has run over today's trip and going before; drawn in stall two and carrying 114 lb, she faces a stiff task on our figures as the lowest-rated runner in the field.

races.paceDynamic: Bymiddaytomorrow is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just one other prominent-style horse (Gerry's Darling) likely to press for position, she should be able to bowl along at a comfortable, uncontested tempo over Thirsk's flat seven furlongs. Gerry's Darling will sit just off the leader's quarters, creating a small two-horse pocket at the head of affairs while the rest of the field organises behind them. The hold-up contingent — Love Tanya, Priscilla's Hope, Bonjour Belle and Spirit of Mary — will need to make significant ground from off the pace, and on a flat, fair track with Good underfoot and no terrain to slow the leader, that is a tall order if Bymiddaytomorrow sets only a moderate gallop. This shape unambiguously favours the prominent-to-lead profile: horses who can track the pace and produce their effort close to the front rather than having to find a clear run late. The field holds more hold-up types than the rear of the map can accommodate; Bonjour Belle and Spirit of Mary, though natural closers, have been redistributed to midfield on the map and are unlikely to find their ideal position in this race, meaning Gerry's Darling is best placed to exploit close proximity to the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Bymiddaytomorrow dictates an unhurried tempo and the hold-up horses are left with too much to find.
scenarios.body: Bymiddaytomorrow skips clear at the two-furlong pole having never faced a serious challenge for the lead, and the gap to the closers is simply too large to bridge on the flat Thirsk straight. Prominent horses who have tracked her closely throughout are the chief beneficiaries, with Gerry's Darling ideally placed to pounce if the leader ties up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Bymiddaytomorrow sets enough pace to tire late, allowing a close-tracking prominent horse to reel her in inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The leader builds a lead through the middle portion of the race but the combination of weight and distance catches up in the final 100 yards, and the closest pursuer sweeps past. Gerry's Darling, with four 7f Good-ground efforts and finishing form over this exact trip, is perfectly profiled to exploit this.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Flier Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to compress the field and allow a closer to weave through for a late surge.
scenarios.body: Love Tanya's form figures of 2-3 at 7f and 6f on Good suggest she has the profile to finish powerfully, and a genuinely strong pace would bring her late run into play more than the map currently suggests. Priscilla's Hope, stepping up from shorter trips, could also find extra when others tire, though the flat track limits the opportunity.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Scrimmage
scenarios.trigger: If there is significant traffic trouble or the race breaks into an unusually fast early pace that scrambles the field order.
scenarios.body: A bunched, unsettled race could theoretically bring redistributed types like Bonjour Belle or Spirit of Mary into contention if gaps appear late, but neither is likely to find their natural hold-up rhythm in this configuration. This is a low-probability disruption scenario only.

watchPoints.text: Gerry's Darling bears close watching: four runs over 7f Good, a recent win, and Kevin Stott in the saddle — if she tracks Bymiddaytomorrow into the straight she is the most dangerous horse in the race.
Bymiddaytomorrow's claimer Ashley Lewis must get her out of the gates promptly — if she is slow away and loses the lead, her entire race plan collapses and her chance is sharply reduced.

Love Tanya is lightly raced (only two runs) and Oisin Orr may try to find a prominent position to compensate for the flat track; watch how she is ridden in the first two furlongs as it signals whether she is being produced positively or held for a late run.

Bonjour Belle and Spirit of Mary are both genuine hold-up horses operating in a congested rear of the field — if either gets a clear outside run from two furlongs out, they could pick up late finishing positions even if a winner's margin is beyond them.
Consultation's 42-day absence is the longest in the field — watch her in the paddock for condition and early market moves, as James Fanshawe horses returning from breaks can sometimes need the run.

races.name: Ladies' Day Saturday 5th September - Book Now Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Qila
runners_data.note: Hold-up style filly returning after 59 days off for Brian Ellison; best form came at 5f on soft/standard ground and the step up to good is not guaranteed to suit, while the long absence adds another layer of uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Qila is hard to fancy, though he has run over today's trip before and a second two starts back offers a crumb of form; 59 days off and 130 lb to carry add to the questions.

runners_data.name: Glory Fighter
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old veteran with a genuine win on good ground over 5f to his name, but his true running style is hold-up and the crowded prominent positions in this field mean he cannot secure a tracking role naturally — he will be further back than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Glory Fighter has finished sixth and unplaced in his last two starts, and with his trainer yet to strike from 23 runners in the past fortnight, it's hard to make a case — despite experience over today's trip and going, and a win four starts back.

runners_data.name: Azuinthejungle
runners_data.note: Four-year-old in fine recent form with two wins from his last three starts, both over the relevant trip; he is a natural prominent racer but with Military Girl and J Street both wanting early positions, he may find himself nudged wider or further back than his form deserves — that positional compromise is the key risk.
runners_data.comment: Azuinthejungle arrives in cracking nick — a winner two starts back and again last time out, fit on just a 10-day turnaround, and with experience of today's trip and conditions. The main risk is that he's up against the top-rated runner in a field of six.

runners_data.name: Vince L'Amour
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has finished no better than sixth in his last five starts on good ground over this trip; the form string offers little encouragement and his similar-going record produces placing rather than winning performances — he needs a dramatically different race shape to feature.
runners_data.comment: Ranked second of six in the field on our figures, Vince L'Amour has run over today's trip and going and arrives fresh on 13 days' rest — yet winless in his last six starts, and a trainer in poor current form at 2/83 is the key concern.

runners_data.name: J Street
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front runner; Billy Garritty has ridden him before and two recent wins at 5f on good and standard ground confirm the style is genuine — the style-fit flag reflects that uncontested leads are never guaranteed, but in a six-runner field he has the best chance of securing the rail.
runners_data.comment: J Street won two starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, with a 13-day turnaround suggesting she arrives fresh and ready; at 135 lb from stall one, the weight burden is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Military Girl
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley's mount arrives with an outstanding profile for this race — three wins from five starts on good ground over 5f, a 52-day break that has not blunted her record, and a style that allows her to track the pace before producing her effort; the highest similar-going score in the field.
runners_data.comment: Military Girl arrives here in fine fettle, a winner twice in her last five starts including back-to-back victories, and she shaped well with a second last time out. She has run over today's trip and going, and a 52-day break shouldn't blunt her edge.

races.paceDynamic: J Street is the one confirmed front runner here and on a flat 5f at Thirsk with just six runners should be able to stride out uncontested at a sustainable gallop, setting a rhythm that suits a sit-and-sprint finish rather than an attritional slog. Military Girl and Azuinthejungle are genuine prominent types who will want to race close to J Street, meaning the early positions behind the leader will be contested rather than handed freely to any one horse. This field contains more pace than the map can formally place — Azuinthejungle and Glory Fighter are genuine prominent and hold-up types respectively who are shown in midfield positions because they cannot all secure their natural ground in this configuration. The resulting shape — one clear leader, two horses pressing for prominent positions, and closers unable to get a clean cart into the race — strongly favours horses that can race prominently or break cleanly from the gate and sustain their effort to the line, particularly those with a confirmed winning record over the course and distance on good ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: J Street Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If J Street breaks cleanly and dictates a true-but-comfortable pace, allowing the prominent horses to time their runs off the leader's back.
scenarios.body: J Street sets a measured tempo and Military Girl, with her excellent record of three wins from a position tracking the pace on good ground, is ideally placed to challenge in the final furlong; the flat Thirsk straight rewards horses who travel prominently and produce a clean turn of foot.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Pressure Bunches Field
scenarios.trigger: If Azuinthejungle pushes hard to assert a prominent spot and creates a truly-run race that compresses the pack.
scenarios.body: A genuinely contested gallop reduces the advantage of the front runners and brings the hold-up horses into play late, giving those furthest back a realistic shot as the leaders tire in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If J Street gets a soft lead and the prominent horses fail to close the gap before the furlong pole.
scenarios.body: J Street's confirmed front-running style and two wins in its recent form string mean an uncontested solo lead on good ground over 5f is not a forlorn hope; a clear break and a solo gallop could see the leader simply never headed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Fliers Arrive Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace collapses or the prominent horses burn each other out and the closers are gifted a finishing run.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires both J Street to fade and the prominent horses to have spent themselves, a low-probability sequence of events; even if it materialises, Glory Fighter and Qila have the profile but the redistribution of true hold-up types to midfield means neither is racing in their genuinely natural position.

watchPoints.text: Military Girl's course-and-distance record on good ground (three wins from the top five) is exceptional for a handicap of this nature and she profiles as the chief danger to the front runner if she travels smoothly in a prominent spot.

Azuinthejungle's redistribution to a midfield map position may cause punters to underestimate how aggressively he tries to press for the front — if he pushes wide early fighting for position, it could cost him ground and energy on the straight.

J Street's STYLE_FIT flag is worth respecting: a prominent horse cast as lone front runner is not the same as a natural, dominant pace-setter, and any stumble from the gates or early challenge from Azuinthejungle/Military Girl could see the lead evaporate quickly.

Glory Fighter at age ten has the widest variation in finishing positions (1st to 15th) in his recent record — his best days on good ground are real but his worst are also on good ground, making him a volatile participant if the race develops unfavourably for true hold-up types.

Trainer Nigel Tinkler has sent out five winners from 27 runners in the last 14 days and Azuinthejungle ran just ten days ago, suggesting the horse is fit and the yard is in form — monitor market moves.

races.name: William Hill, Market Place, Thirsk Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Master Vintner
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's 4yo has strong course and distance form (2nd on STA, 1st over 12f on STA), returns after 36 days, and is the only natural front-runner here — style fit is high for leading but the STYLE_FIT tag reflects he has been mapped as prominent rather than a confirmed leader, so fractionally temper confidence if rivals pressurise him early.
runners_data.comment: Consecutive runner-up finishes on his two most recent starts paint Master Vintner as a horse in excellent heart, and a winner five starts back underlines his ability. He has run over today's distance and going, and 36 days off shouldn't blunt his edge carrying 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Majestic
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's well-travelled 8yo is a deep hold-up performer with his last win coming over a similar trip on good ground, but a record of 10th last time out over this exact distance and surface suggests he needs everything to go right at the business end; Connor Beasley will be patient and look for a gap.
runners_data.comment: Majestic was second two starts back, and he has run over today's distance and going before — at 132 lb he carries plenty of weight, which is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Wahdan
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 5yo races in a hood and has shown fair form at 12f on good ground, finishing 3rd most recently over that trip; David Allan will hunt cover from the rear and the horse needs a strong pace to deliver his effort, which looks unlikely given only one confirmed pace-setter.
runners_data.comment: Wahdan steps back up looking for a first win in recent starts, but he's shown enough with a third last time out and has run over today's trip and going — his rating of 97 tops this field. The worry is a trainer in the depths of a lean spell at just 2%.

runners_data.name: Sudu
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's 4yo returns from a 373-day absence and will need this run to sharpen fitness, but his one career victory came over 12f on good ground and Ray Dawson will aim to sit prominently just off Master Vintner — his natural prominent style puts him in a strong positional berth if fresh enough to land a blow.
runners_data.comment: A lengthy absence of 373 days makes Sudu very hard to trust on return, and eighth last time out does him no favours; he has run over today's trip and going, and the trainer's 37% strike rate over 14 days offers a rare crumb of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Wanderlust
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's 4yo has an unknown style tag but recent form suggests a handy, mid-to-prominent placement suits, finishing 3rd and 4th in recent efforts at 10-12f on good and soft; Andrew Mullen should have options to stalk the pace and his consistency makes him a reliable each-way threat if the race is run at a comfortable tempo.
runners_data.comment: Wanderlust showed a return to form with a win four starts back and was placed third last time out, and his going experience is a clear asset at 127 lb; the concern is a 43-day absence that leaves his sharpness open to question.

runners_data.name: Golden West
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 5yo is a genuine hold-up performer whose true style sees him closing from the rear, but he has been mapped to midfield here because the field has more hold-up types than the rear positions can accommodate — Duran Fentiman will need to find a rhythm from wherever he settles, and his best recent effort (2nd over 11f on good) came from a truly run race; the style displacement tempers his prospects.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a tame ninth last time out, Golden West is a tough one to fancy at the foot of our rankings — though he has run over today's trip and going before, and at least returns here fresh enough at 28 days since his last run.

races.paceDynamic: Master Vintner is the only confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and, with no rival likely to seriously challenge for the lead over 1m4f on good ground at Thirsk, he should dictate a sustainable, metronomic gallop from the front. Sudu and Wanderlust are both prominent-minded types who will press close to the pace but neither has the profile or inclination to turn this into a true test, meaning the tempo is likely to be controlled rather than searching. With the pace well-managed and no genuine pressure expected, the race sets up as a target on Master Vintner's back from a modest fractions scenario that rewards horses travelling comfortably mid-race and producing a clean, well-timed surge in the final quarter-mile. This shape favours prominent or handy runners who can stalk the leader without burning fuel — Sudu and Wanderlust are best-placed positionally, while the hold-up brigade face a more open road to a winning position if the pace is honest enough, but on current indications they will need something to go wrong in front rather than simply finishing through.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Master Vintner Controls Solo
scenarios.trigger: If Master Vintner gets to the front uncontested and sets a gentle, unchallenged gallop, the race becomes a test of cruising efficiency and a late kick rather than raw stamina.
scenarios.body: Master Vintner dictates every inch at a pace of his own choosing, and horses travelling prominently like Sudu and Wanderlust are ideally placed to pounce when he is challenged or tires; hold-up runners face too much ground to make up if the tempo never truly wounds the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finishers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is honest enough to string the field out and expose the leader in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Majestic or Wahdan close from the rear under patient rides as the pace-set leader weakens, benefiting from a genuine end-to-end test; this scenario requires the tempo to be faster than expected given only one natural front-runner.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Duel Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If Sudu or Wanderlust push forward early to contest the lead and the pace lifts into a genuine contest.
scenarios.body: A more pressured gallop stretches the hold-up horses and suits the winner coming from a prominent or handy berth; Master Vintner risks being emptied if pressed harder than ideal over this trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Tactical Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so slow that the whole field bunches entering the straight and it becomes a sprint finish over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A slow-run race with a late dash benefits the horse with the sharpest finishing effort regardless of positional style; Golden West, though a genuine hold-up type placed in a redistributed midfield position in the map, would need everything to fall perfectly and a strong finishing effort from the pack.

watchPoints.text: Master Vintner sets the pace unchallenged — watch whether Sudu or Wanderlust push forward before the first bend, as any early pressure on the lone front-runner would reshape the entire pace scenario.

Golden West is a genuine hold-up horse mapped to midfield due to redistribution — watch whether Duran Fentiman can find a natural rhythm from a compressed starting position or whether he gets shuffled further back than ideal.
Sudu's 373-day absence is a significant fitness unknown — watch the betting market for late confidence signals from the Roger Varian yard before assuming he runs to his pre-layoff form on debut back.

With six runners over 1m4f on a flat, galloping track in good conditions, watch whether the entire field is still tightly grouped turning into the straight, which would signal a pace that has been too slow to truly sort out the hold-up horses.
Wahdan's headgear (hood) and a recent run just 13 days ago suggests Easterby is sharpening him for a performance — watch whether he tracks up closer than his hold-up tag implies in the early stages.

races.name: Country Music Night Here Next Friday 14th August Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Hellcat
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse placed into midfield due to overcrowding at the rear; Ross Burdon's filly has mixed sprint form and only 5 wins-or-places from 8 runs in similar ground — limited scope to win from a compromised position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Hellcat faces a stiff ask here; the third three starts back is a flicker of ability, and she has run over today's trip and going, but the overall profile makes her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Lope Y Linda
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's filly steps back to 6f after a string of placed efforts over 7f-8f in Good going; prominent style suits this pace shape and David Allan's local course knowledge is an asset, though the drop to sprinting may catch her out late.
runners_data.comment: Lope Y Linda was a winner four starts back and arrives here on a quick 16-day turnaround with distance and going experience in her favour, but consecutive fourths in her last two runs and a trainer in poor form (2%) are real concerns at 124 lb from stall 6.

runners_data.name: Liquid Cooled
runners_data.note: A genuine closer whose natural role is at the rear of the field; Ben Haslam's gelding won over 6f at Southwell but has only one place from seven Good-going runs — the crowded midfield mapping further reduces his chance of finding daylight.
runners_data.comment: Ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Liquid Cooled has disappointed in his last three starts — fifth most recently — and rates hard to fancy at the weights, though he has run over today's trip before and the 21-day break at least suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Agric Ranger
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby runner with a hold-up pedigree who simply lacks the form to win from any position — five runs without a win or place in similar ground, and being shuffled into midfield out of role only compounds the problem.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, Agric Ranger faces a stiff ask here — a trainer striking at just 2% in the last 14 days does little to encourage confidence, though he has run over today's trip before and goes from stall three.

runners_data.name: Overbudget
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's prominent-racing gelding carries top weight but has run consistently at 6f and showed a place effort in Good going recently; if he can get the drop off Yellow Diamonds cleanly, his prominent style is ideally suited to Scenario A.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Overbudget at least posted a third three starts back, though sixth and seventh in more recent outings temper expectations; a trainer firing at just 3% and 42 days off the track are further checks on enthusiasm despite experience over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Real Jack
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley takes over for Michael Dods and this horse's prominent style fits the race shape, though a run of five consecutive single-figure finishes without hitting the frame at 6f makes him a shape-suited runner rather than a compelling winning proposition.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Real Jack does at least bring a second five starts back and handles today's distance and going; our rating of 75 gives him a solid profile edge, and 48 days between runs should leave him fresh stepping off a mark of 62.

runners_data.name: Soul Warrior
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's gelding carries an explicit finishing fade warning; Alex Jary (3lb claimer) rode him to a place at 6f in Good going but the ⚠ flag is significant — a race run at even a mildly honest pace will expose his tendency to weaken.
runners_data.comment: Soul Warrior showed a third two starts back but has been out of the frame more often than not in recent starts; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 128 lb from stall 11, and an 18-day absence leaves fitness just a shade uncertain.

runners_data.name: Mare Of London
runners_data.note: Sam James takes the ride on Mark Walford's filly, who is a natural hold-up performer pushed forward into midfield by virtue of a congested field; six runs since last win and no Good-going wins suggest she needs things to fall perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Mare Of London has been finding the frame difficult of late, but her second **five starts back** shows she can threaten at this level, and distance-and-going experience plus a sharp 14-day turnaround keep her firmly in the mix; the risk is she's been winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Maximum Velocity
runners_data.note: Highest OR in the field at 65 with headgear noted; Tinkler/McManoman combination has placed this filly twice at 6f in Good going including a win at 7f, and her recent figures are strong — though her hold-up style means she needs a clear passage to land a blow.
runners_data.comment: Maximum Velocity arrives on the back of a runner-up finish last time out, and he has distance and going experience to call upon here. The chief concern is that his nine starts back showed a tendency to disappoint, and 135 lb is a stiff burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Yellow Diamonds
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's lone front-runner who gets to dictate from the front unchallenged; the STYLE_FIT flag reflects the step up from 5f where she has consistently run well, and the key question is whether 6f in Good going exposes her stamina in the final furlong.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Yellow Diamonds nonetheless catches the eye with her consistent run of fourth-place finishes — four starts back, three starts back, and two starts back — and she has experience of today's distance and going; at 134 lb from stall 10, the weight could be the sticking point.

runners_data.name: Great Profit
runners_data.note: W H Harrison's gelding arrives fresh (11 days) on the back of three consecutive runner-up efforts at 5f-6f in Good and similar going; a genuine hold-up type whose form at the trip is the best in the race on a placed-run basis, and he looks best equipped of the closers if any scenario opens up late.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without being a winner, Great Profit has finished second in each of his last three starts yet is winless in recent starts, with the eighth four starts back a concern. Suited by today's distance and going, he returns quickly after 11 days and carries 133 lb from stall five.

races.paceDynamic: Yellow Diamonds is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival willing to press from the outside, should be allowed to dictate a controlled, honest gallop across the six furlongs at Thirsk. Overbudget and Real Jack are the two most likely horses to sit just off the pace in a genuine prominent position, giving the race a settled, single-file look through the first half. This field is deceptively loaded with hold-up horses — Hellcat, Liquid Cooled, Agric Ranger and Mare Of London are all true come-from-behind types who cannot all find their natural position at the rear and will be pushed into midfield, meaning the back straight will be congested and the finishers will need a clear run that may not materialise. The dominant race shape here favours the prominent racer who can sit two or three lengths off Yellow Diamonds, travel comfortably through the race, and produce a sustained challenge in the final two furlongs — hold-up horses are structurally compromised in this setup.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Yellow Diamonds sets an uncontested, measured gallop and the prominent horses behind track efficiently without burning fuel.
scenarios.body: Yellow Diamonds dictates from the front on a true surface in Good going, setting a pace that is fair but never suicidal, with Overbudget or Real Jack sitting poised to pounce entering the final furlong; the shape rewards horses who race close to the action rather than those hunting from deep. Maximum Velocity, who has winning form at the trip in Good going and good recent figures, is well placed to exploit this shape if her hold-up style allows her to land close enough.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Rush
scenarios.trigger: If Yellow Diamonds goes too hard early under pressure and ties up in the final furlong, opening the race up for closers.
scenarios.body: A contested or slightly too-strong early gallop would see the front end weaken sharply inside the final furlong, giving the deeper horses a rare opportunity to come through; Great Profit, with three consecutive runner-up finishes including twice at 6f in Good, would be the primary beneficiary. Maximum Velocity's closing ability and strong Good-going record give her relevance here too, though her redistribution to midfield moderates expectations.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Slowdown, Few Involved
scenarios.trigger: If Yellow Diamonds produces a crawl in the early stages and the race only ignites turning into the straight.
scenarios.body: A stop-start gallop on this flat track would compress the field and create a sprint finish where positional luck and a turn of foot become decisive; Lope Y Linda, who has placed at 7f-8f in Good going and shows tactical versatility, could benefit from her prominent style in a race that suddenly becomes a six-furlong dash over the final two furlongs. Yellow Diamonds remains dangerous if she can quicken from a slow pace, but the field bunching up hands chances to horses that might otherwise be outpaced.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide Draw, Traffic Trouble
scenarios.trigger: If pace-congested midfield causes interference in the straight and true hold-up horses are blocked, elevating those with a clean passage.
scenarios.body: With Hellcat, Liquid Cooled, Agric Ranger and Mare Of London all crowded into midfield rather than at the rear where they belong, traffic jams are a genuine risk and any horse drawn wide enough to avoid trouble could grab an unlikely prize. Great Profit's consistent recent placed efforts at 6f in Good going make him the most resilient option if the straight becomes chaotic, but this is the lowest-probability shape and dependent on a sequence of misfortunes for others.

watchPoints.text: Yellow Diamonds' stamina at 6f is the pivotal factor — she is stepping up from 5f and if she ties up in the final furlong the entire race shape collapses.

Midfield congestion is a structural risk: Hellcat, Liquid Cooled, Agric Ranger and Mare Of London are all pushed out of their natural hold-up position, creating a bunched centre-track group that could cause interference in the straight.

Great Profit arrives on a quick turnaround of 11 days having finished second in each of his last three outings — watch whether trainer W H Harrison has sent him here to win or fill a place, as his form makes him dangerous if fresh.

Maximum Velocity wears headgear and is trained by the in-form Nigel Tinkler yard (5 winners from 27 in 14 days); her Good-going figures are the most consistent in the race and she is worth monitoring in the market.

Tim Easterby saddles two runners (Lope Y Linda and Agric Ranger) — David Allan takes the prominent type while Duran Fentiman rides the hold-up horse, suggesting stable confidence may sit with Lope Y Linda in this pace shape.
